title: What the study could have missed: errors, power, and the cost of testing everything

objectives.statement: Distinguish a Type I error from a Type II error by stating what each decision got wrong, say which of the two probabilities an investigator chooses and when, and identify which error a described failure represents.
Calculate the power of a stated two-group design against a stated true effect, from a standard deviation, a sample size, and a significance level, and state the Type II error rate that goes with it.

Predict the direction in which power moves when the true effect, the sample size, the measurement variability, or the significance level changes, and calculate both the effect a design could detect with 80% power and the sample size a stated effect would require.
Judge what a study reporting no difference has established, using its confidence interval and its power against a named effect, and rewrite an over-reaching conclusion into one the design supports.

Calculate the probability that at least one of several independent comparisons crosses a threshold when none is real, choose a per-comparison threshold that holds a target family-wise rate, and state the power that adjustment costs.
